title: The Fritz band with Bunk Johnson and the 1919 move to New Orleans
summary: Ernie names the members of the band his brother played in with Bunk Johnson, which played at ship launchings in World War I. Earl Foster and Andrew Anderson also came from Madisonville, and in 1919 he moved to New Orleans with his brother.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And you remember anything about the band that Bung was in? Who was the band?

Oh yes. Who else? Matter of fact, I have a sister-in-law that his wife, my brother's wife has the picture of the band, but I've been trying to get it for him. And I'm Trill's time to get it for him. She lives on Orleans Street. And I hope someday she will let me have it. And in that band, the leader of the band was Joe Fritz, the daddy, he played bass. And one of the brothers was Earl Fritz, he played the trombone. And Isidore Fritz was a piano player, also was the teacher of George Lewis.
Yeah, George has told us about him a little bit.
And Leon Pyron was the guitar player. And my brother played drums and Bung Johnson was the trumpet player.
Earl Foster told us a little bit about that band, he mentioned you too.

Yeah, well he lived in Maddenville, you see. And every time that Janker would launch a ship during World War I, 1917 in the Shifunksu River, they would come and play for the luncheon of the ship. And when they'd come and do that, well they'd always stay home, see. But during the time they were home they'd rehearsal and they'd play joys from, leave from my house and play right around those little country towns like that. And he would come back there. And in 1919, my brother came here to live and I came with him.
Did you know Andy Anderson over that part of the country too?
Andrew Anderson, yeah he lived in Maddenville too, Earl Foster, he's from Maddenville. A cousin I believe was there. Yeah, first cousin Earl Foster.
He told us he heard Bung too when he was a kid.
